tagline: Up onto the bluff tops, where the orchards are.
intro: From La Crescent, County Highway 29 heads up onto the bluff tops and runs north through rolling farmland high above the Mississippi valley, until it comes back down to Highway 61, the Great River Road, which meets it at both ends. Orchards along the way sell apples, cider and pumpkins.

The apples began in La Crescent with John S. Harris, who planted the area's first trees in 1857 in spite of the belief, held by 99 people out of 100, that apples could not grow in Minnesota. He tried hundreds of varieties until he had trees hardy enough for the winters. Half of them, he said, were total failures.

moments.title: La Crescent
moments.text: One of its founders, Peter Cameron, set out to dig a canal turning the Mississippi toward his town and away from La Crosse, and died ten weeks before it was due to be finished.

moments.title: Dakota
moments.text: Laid out in 1855 by Nathan Brown, who ran a ferry across to Wisconsin, the town was once the center of berry growing and grows apples now.

moments.title: Great River Bluffs State Park
moments.text: Short paths lead out to overlooks from bluffs 500 feet above the river, and to goat prairies, grass on slopes so steep it seems only goats could graze them.
